title: I rented a basement apartment cheap. The previous tenant left a note on the fridge. Rule one: never answer the second knock.
transcript:
I rented a basement apartment cheap. The previous tenant left a note on the fridge. Rule one: never answer the second knock. The landlord only charged four hundred dollars a month, and he wouldn't look at me when he handed over the key.

The note was on the fridge, written in careful block letters. Rule one said never answer the second knock. Rule two said the first knock is always the mailman. Rule three said if you hear your own voice on the stairs, stay in bed.

I took it as a joke left by a bored college kid. Then, around midnight, somebody knocked. One slow knock. I didn't move.

The next night there was one knock again, and a minute later a second knock, softer, from the closet inside the apartment.

I did not answer. I lay there with my heart in my throat while the closet door creaked, slowly, open.

The third night, I heard my own voice on the stairs. It said, "It's okay, you can come out now. I'm the one who lives here."

I stayed in bed like the note said. In the morning, I found a fourth rule I hadn't seen before, written in my handwriting, on the back of the note.

It said, "Rule four, you are not the first tenant."

Then came a knock.
